extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO examiners handling continuation/divisional/CPA filings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive filing/processing requirements for continuation, divisional, and Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) practice under 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(d), including interactions with RCE practice and requirements for affidavits/declarations, fees, signatures, filing dates, and new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations from prior application in 37 CFR 1.53(b) continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations (e.g., those submitted under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131 and 1.132) filed during prosecution of the prior application do not automatically become a part of a continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where it is desired to rely on an earlier filed affidavit or declaration, the applicant should make the remarks of record in this application and include a copy of the original affidavit or declaration filed in the prior application. Examiner Note: Do not use the form paragraph for applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) since affidavits/declarations filed during prosecution of the parent nonprovisional application automatically become a part of the 37 CFR 1.53(d) application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for establishing continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior application and the continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the petition for an extension of time must be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3), an authorization to charge required fees will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for an extension. Petition directed to the prior application must be accompanied by its own certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 (if mailed by first class mail) or under 37 CFR 1.10 (if mailed by Express Mail) if those benefits are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of prior nonprovisional not automatic (37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(b) and 37 CFR 1.63(d) practice, the prior nonprovisional application is not automatically abandoned upon filing of the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior application is to be expressly abandoned, such a paper must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.138. A registered patent practitioner not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34 may also expressly abandon the prior nonprovisional application as of the filing date granted to a continuing application when filing such a continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of issue fee payment on abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior nonprovisional application which is to be expressly abandoned has a notice of allowance issued, the prior application can become abandoned by the nonpayment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, once an issue fee has been paid in the prior application, even if the payment occurs following the filing of a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a petition to withdraw the prior nonprovisional application from issue must be filed before the prior application can be abandoned (37 CFR 1.313). See MPEP § 711.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying the Board of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior nonprovisional application which is to be expressly abandoned is before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, a separate notice should be forwarded by the appellant to the Board giving them notice of the abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination — preliminary amendments and amendment compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any preliminary amendment present on the filing date of an application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) is part of the original disclosure; amendments must be filed in compliance with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, the amendment must include a complete claim listing whenever a claim is added, canceled, or amended. Applications should be classified and assigned to the proper Technology Center by taking into consideration the claims that will be before the examiner upon entry of such a preliminary amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when copy of prior oath/declaration contains new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a copy of the oath or declaration from a prior application was filed in a continuation or divisional application and the examiner determines that new matter is present relative to the prior application, the examiner should so notify the applicant in the next Office action (preferably the first Office action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should require: (A) a new oath or declaration along with the surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(f); and (B) that the application be redesignated as a continuation-in-part. See MPEP § 608.04(b) when new matter is contained in a preliminary amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing pages/drawings for continuations/divisionals filed before 9/21/2004
rubrics_metrics.description: If pages of the specification or drawing figures described in the specification are missing and the application is a continuation or divisional filed prior to Sept 21, 2004 under 37 CFR 1.53(b) using a copy of the oath/declaration filed in the prior application under 37 CFR 1.63(d), the examiner must check whether the continuation/divisional includes a statement incorporating by reference the prior application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of incorporation by reference was necessary to permit applicant to amend the continuation/divisional to include subject matter in the prior application(s) without the need for a petition. If the continuation/divisional does not include the incorporation statement and applicant has not been informed of omitted items, the application should be returned to OIPE for mailing of a 'Notice of Omitted Item(s).' For apps filed on or after Sept 21, 2004, see 37 CFR 1.57(a) and MPEP § 201.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA filing eligibility — design application requirement (37 CFR 1.53(d)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application (but not a continuation-in-part) of a prior nonprovisional application may be filed as a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) provided that the application is for a design patent and the prior nonprovisional application is a design application complete as defined by § 1.51(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CPA is available only for design applications that meet the completeness requirements of 37 CFR 1.51(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA filing deadline conditions (37 CFR 1.53(d)(1)(ii)/(ii(A)-(C)))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) must be filed before the earliest of: (A) payment of the issue fee on the prior application (unless a petition under § 1.313(c) is granted), (B) abandonment of the prior application, or (C) termination of proceedings on the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA filing date definition (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a continued prosecution application is the date on which a request on a separate paper for an application under this paragraph is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for a CPA cannot be submitted as part of papers filed for another purpose (e.g., within an amendment after final).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA must identify the prior application (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) must identify the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification can be by application number (series code and serial number) or by serial number and filing date. Applicant is urged to also furnish title of invention, name of applicants, and correspondence address in the CPA request (37 CFR 1.53(d)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA subject matter limitation (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA discloses and claims only subject matter disclosed in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment in a CPA may introduce new matter or matter that would have been new matter in the prior application. Any new specification filed with the CPA request will be treated as a substitute specification under § 1.125 and is not part of the original application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship requirement for CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)(iii)/(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA must name as inventors the same inventors named in the prior application on the date the CPA was filed, except as provided in paragraph (d)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed under this paragraph may be filed by fewer than all the inventors named in the prior application provided the request is accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the name(s) of persons who are not inventors of the invention being claimed in the new application. No person may be named as an inventor in a CPA who was not named as an inventor in the prior application on the date the CPA was filed, except by correction under § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA uses prior file jacket and identification number (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPA request will utilize the file jacket and contents of the prior application, including specification, drawings and oath/declaration from the prior application, to constitute the new application, and will be assigned the application number of the prior application for identification purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA is a request to expressly abandon the prior application (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) is a request to expressly abandon the prior application as of the filing date of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to expressly abandon is not effective until the abandonment is acknowledged upon processing and entry of the CPA into the file of the prior application. If applicant does not want the prior application abandoned, they must file under 37 CFR 1.53(b) instead or file a timely petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to change treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA fees (37 CFR 1.53(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing fee, search fee, and examination fee for a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) are the basic filing fee as set forth in § 1.16(b), the search fee as set forth in § 1.16(l), and the examination fee as set forth in § 1.16(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: No search and examination fees were required for a CPA filed before December 8, 2004, but current statutory requirements apply for CPAs filed after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in CPAs; handling substitute specifications (37 CFR 1.53(d)(5) and § 1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new change must be made in the form of an amendment to the prior application as it existed prior to the filing of a CPA. No amendment in a CPA may introduce new matter. Any new specification filed with the CPA request will be treated as a substitute specification in accordance with § 1.125.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification must comply with § 1.125(b) and be accompanied by a statement that it includes no new matter. A substitute specification containing new matter will be denied entry by the examiner. Any new matter which is entered will be required to be canceled pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 132 from the descriptive portion of the specification, and any claims relying on such new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. Applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting that the substitute specification or preliminary amendment be removed from the CPA file and treated as a separate application, but a refund of the CPA filing fee is not available simply because such a petition is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA chain and pendency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA may be based on a prior CPA so long as the prior CPA is complete under 37 CFR 1.51(b) and is a design application. There is no other limit to the number of CPAs that may be filed in a chain of continuing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, only one CPA may be pending at one time based on the same prior nonprovisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original disclosure and new-matter carryover into CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The original disclosure of a CPA is the same as the original disclosure of the parent non-continued prosecution application and amendments entered in the parent application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subject matter added by amendment in the parent application which is deemed to be new matter in the parent application will also be considered new matter in the CPA. No amendment filed in a CPA, even if filed on the filing date of the CPA, may include new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of papers as CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: If application papers for a design application are in any way designated as a CPA filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (e.g., contain a reference to 37 CFR 1.53(d), CPA, or continued prosecution application), the application papers will be treated by the Office as a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), even if the papers also contain other inconsistent designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, if papers for a utility or plant application are designated as a CPA filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the papers will be treated as a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 because CPA practice was eliminated for utility and plant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA practice eliminated for utility and plant applications (effective July 14, 2003)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 14, 2003, CPA practice has been eliminated as to utility and plant applications; applicants who wish to continue examination of the same claimed invention after prosecution is closed should consider filing a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs filed prior to July 14, 2003 will continue to be processed under prior 37 CFR 1.53(d). Any CPA filed on or after July 14, 2003 in a utility or plant application is improper regardless of the filing date of the utility or plant application in which the CPA is filed. The Office will not convert an improper CPA into an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) unless the applicant shows extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper CPA in utility/plant applications depending on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a utility or plant application has a filing date on or after June 8, 1995, an improper CPA filed on or after July 14, 2003 will be treated as a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114. If the utility or plant application has a filing date before June 8, 1995, the Office cannot treat an improper CPA filed on or after July 14, 2003 as an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If treated as improper and not converted, the Office will notify applicant by mailing a Notice of Improper CPA (or FWC) Filing and the time period for reply set in the last Office action will continue to run. If the time period has expired, the application is abandoned and the applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application (with required fees and submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA filed in error — examiner action
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner discovers that an improper or incomplete CPA has been processed as a proper CPA in error, the examiner should immediately notify a supervisory applications examiner or other technical support staff within the Technology Center who will reprocess the CPA and correct the application records as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checks for CPA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA request will be initially processed by the Technology Center assigned the prior application, which will verify that (A) the prior application is a design application, (B) the correct prior application number is identified in the request, (C) the request is properly signed, (D) the prior application was pending on, and that the issue fee has not been paid in the prior application on or prior to, the filing date of the CPA request, (E) the prior application was complete under 37 CFR 1.51(b) (e.g., filing fee paid and a signed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 filed), and (F) the proper filing fee has been paid in the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more conditions have not been satisfied or the proper fees have not been paid, the applicant will be notified and no examination will be made until the error is corrected or proper fees submitted. See 37 CFR 1.53(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect prior application number identified — TC procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA request does not properly identify the prior application number, the Technology Center should attempt to identify the proper application number by reference to other identifying information (e.g., inventor name, filing date, title, docket number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the TC identifies the correct number, it should be entered on the CPA request and dated/initialed. If unable to identify and the submitter is a registered practitioner, the practitioner may be requested to supply a signed letter with the correct number. If all attempts fail, the paper requesting the CPA should be returned to the sender with a cover letter indicating that resubmission with the correct number within two weeks will preserve the original date of receipt. The two-week period is not extendible. Applicants may use Certificate of Mailing or Express Mail procedures to preserve deposit date for resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for CPA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is a request to expressly abandon the prior application and therefore must be properly signed; for listing of who may sign see 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a joint application with no attorney or agent, all applicants must sign the CPA request for it to be effective to abandon. An unsigned or improperly signed CPA request will be placed in the file of the prior application and is entitled to an application filing date but is ineffective to abandon the prior application. A CPA will not be examined until the CPA request is properly signed. A registered practitioner acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 may sign; an assignee may sign if accompanied by papers establishing ownership under 37 CFR 3.73(b), unless such papers were already filed in the prior application and ownership has not changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA filing date and permitted filing methods (including facsimile rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a CPA is the date on which a request on a separate paper for a CPA is filed. A paper requesting a CPA may be sent by mail, by facsimile transmission, or filed directly at the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of receipt for a facsimile transmission is the date the complete transmission is received by an Office facsimile unit, unless completed on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in DC, in which case the receipt date is the next succeeding non-holiday. Applicants may include a 'Receipt for Facsimile Transmitted CPA' (PTO/SB/29A) which will be separated, date-stamped and returned to the provided mailing address; such receipt cannot acknowledge papers other than the CPA request and the USPTO will not retain the receipt in the application file. Returned receipt may be prima facie evidence of filing by facsimile on the stamped date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to file preliminary amendments with CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly encouraged to file any preliminary amendment in a CPA at the time the CPA is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office treats CPAs that are 'amended' applications (when the prior application had an Office action) as having examination priority similar to amended applications, resulting in a shorter timeframe to the first Office action than for 'new' applications. See 37 CFR 1.115 and MPEP § 714.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of improper CPA being treated as improper RCE or vice versa
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA is improper (e.g., missing required fees or submission) and is treated as an improper RCE, the Office will send a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE), PTO-2051, and the time period set in the last Office action will continue to run. If the time period has expired, the application is abandoned and a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 is required to revive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot, as a matter of right, obtain continued examination on claims that are independent and distinct from the invention previously claimed (i.e., cannot switch inventions when filing an RCE). If a divisional CPA is filed improperly and is treated as an RCE and the newly submitted claims are directed to an invention distinct from the previously claimed invention, such claims will be withdrawn from consideration and applicant should be notified using appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 8.26 or 8.27).
